questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The beautiful nature of Northern Ireland, the English language, the courses avaliable at the university, the student accommodation, all the facilities the university offered, and the opportunity to discover the Northern Irish culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. There was a reception at the accommodation site.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I talked to someone at the reception close to my accommodation and was able to ask questions, receive my key, buy a kitchen pack etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: “Elms Village” where you lived with (mostly oher Erasmus) students

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a kitchen at my accommodation and you were able to buy a kitchen pack with the necessities to cook

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is very nice to live on campus with other students. And that you need to be quick with applying for it so the opportunity doesn’t get lost

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to fill out some information, have your picture taken, and receive a Student ID with which you could enter the library etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The reception at my accommodation was almost always open and ready to help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The website of the university had by mistake not been updated so I only got one out of three of my requested classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To make sure you know what is needed regarding your Visa. And ask other students or any avaliable student support facility if you are in doubt about anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It seemed a lot easier than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot more contact and support offered to the students

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and the law
International criminal and transitional justice
European constiutional law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of my courses as I found all of them very refreshing and interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mostly just all the souvenirs I wanted to buy :-)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most items - like food, transportation, beauty and health products - were all less expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of these opportunities: many with Irish food tasting, afternoon tea, pizza nights, Irish music, baking, painting… It was very impressive!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them. Particularly the ones going on field trips, seeing the beautiful nature of Northern Ireland, food events where you can chat with others, and the more creative ones.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I especially recommend seeing Giant’s Causeway, Rathlin Island, Derry, Portrush, Dunluce Castle, and Glenariff Waterfall Park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The creative or active events will probably especially makes this easier as you can comment on what you are doing and bond over something

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly that the Northern Irish men were very direct and forward when approaching you and flirting with you

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The music, the appreciation of nature, the Irish fairytales and litterature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don’t hold back! Be yourself and join as many events as possible. If you still haven’t found your best friend, don’t give up, and don’t be scared to start conversations as you are only away for such a short time. A more practical advice would be to get a card for the public transport, get the Value Cab app, and stay safe in the nightlife - never leave your drink unattended.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you also come to a dorm-like accommodation with other student, I’d recommend making a plan to share everything that you all need - spices, salt, pepper, cleaning supplies, oil, sauces… it makes everything a lot easier and reduces waste!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The beautiful nature, the feeling of independence and finding my way, the academic enrichment, and most of all the incredible people that I met and hope to hold onto for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was getting over some unpleasant nights out where my boundaries were crossed

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
